chunks: 30 - Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from al-Mithammi from Zurarah ibn A'yan and Dawud ibn Sirhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Abdullah ibn Bukayr from Udaym, the seller of al-Harawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

«The mu'lana (one who performs li'an) does not become permissible to his wife forever. And the one who marries the woman during her waiting period while he knows it is not permissible to him forever. And the one who divorces her with the divorce of 'not permissible until she marries another husband' three times, and marries her three times, does not become permissible to her forever. And the one who is in ihram if he marries while he knows it is forbidden for him, does not become permissible to her forever».

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The one in the state of ihram (ritual consecration) for Hajj or Umrah.
key_terms.الْمُلَاعَنَةُ: Li'an, the mutual imprecation between husband and wife to accuse each other of false adultery, resulting in separation.
key_terms.حَتَّى تَنْكِحَ زَوْجاً غَيْرَهُ: Until she marries another husband, a condition for the validity of the third divorce.
key_terms.عِدَّتِهَا: Her waiting period (iddah) after divorce or death.
key_terms.لاَ تَحِلُّ لَهُ أَبَداً: It does not become permissible to him forever, indicating permanent invalidity.

ai.seo_question: What are the four cases where a marriage becomes permanently invalid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details four specific causes of permanent prohibition (haram al-muwallad) in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that these barriers are irreversible unlike temporary prohibitions. It highlights the distinct legal weight of *li'an* (mutual imprecation), marriage during the *iddah* with knowledge, triple conditional divorce, and marriage in *ihram* with knowledge, distinguishing them from standard divorce mechanics. The narration underscores the finality of these states, ensuring clarity in marital eligibility for the community.
